basis: Defined by craniosynostosis and structural abnormalities of thumbs, fingers and toes; shallow orbits alone do not establish ocular dysfunction.
Malignant smooth muscle tumour arising in the liver; no evidence that infection defines this concept.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; strabismus and ptosis each occur in 30-79%; characteristic skeletal anomalies include arthrogryposis in 2/2 assessed patients.
Autoimmune thrombotic coagulopathy with frequent hemolysis; renal microangiopathic injury in ~70%. Common pulmonary and neurologic injury omitted under the four-axis cap.
Neoplasm of the pituitary endocrine gland; visual or neurologic compression is not universal across this tumour umbrella.
Pathologically dilated veins within the oesophagus define both the gastrointestinal location and vascular disease; underlying liver disease is separate.
Defined by cerebral cortical malformation with cerebellar and brainstem hypoplasia.
Hydranencephaly and congenital structural deficiency of the diaphragm define the syndrome; associated cardiac defects and pulmonary hypertension lack frequency evidence.
Inherited ichthyosis characterized by abnormal cutaneous keratinization; no common extracutaneous damage established across the group.
Severe developmental impairment defines it; cardiac, GI and skeletal malformations are described as common. Unspecified urogenital anomalies do not establish renal involvement.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with progressive dystonia, dyskinesia and severe intellectual disability.
Malignant neoplasm occupying the kidney; distant organ involvement is not defining across the umbrella.
Obstetric disorder of the chorioamniotic membranes; no covered organ is intrinsically affected.
Psychiatric body dysmorphic disorder; perceived inadequate muscularity does not indicate skeletal muscle disease.
Progressive macular and retinal dystrophy causing impaired colour, night and peripheral vision.
Inherited cholestatic metabolic disease with cirrhosis in 5/5; intrinsic glomerulosclerosis in 2/2 assessed and developmental delay in 3/3 support renal and neurologic involvement.
Intellectual disability in 80-99%; skeletal malformations in 30-79%. Eye/ear findings lack evidence of functional damage; kidney abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Acquired benign blood vessel neoplasm; no particular anatomical site is specified.
Inherited susceptibility to chronic cutaneous HPV infection with persistent skin lesions; subsequent skin cancer is a separate disease.
Congenital attachment restricting tongue movement; tongue and floor of mouth fall within the gastrointestinal axis.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder with demyelinating neuropathy; progressive distal muscle atrophy and functional loss are characteristic. Hearing loss frequency is unclear.
Partial loss of colour vision is an ocular functional disorder.
Defined by developmental impairment and dental anomalies; developmental delay affects 35/36 and intellectual disability 28/31 assessed patients. Teeth are gastrointestinal.
Malignant smooth muscle tumour arising in the lung; no evidence that infection defines this concept.
Mosaic Legius syndrome presents with localized pigmentary skin abnormalities; common damage to other covered organs is not established.
